hints: Notice the given law $I = P/(4\pi r^2)$ with constant $P$, so intensity $I$ is proportional to $1/r^2$.
Connect intensity to amplitude using $I \propto a^2$ for a wave of constant frequency in the same medium.
Combine the two proportionalities to get $a^2 \propto 1/r^2$, then take the square root to find how $a$ depends on $r$.
walkthrough: Identify the spreading law: $I = P/(4\pi r^2)$. With $P$ constant, $I \propto 1/r^2$ because the same power crosses sphere area $4\pi r^2$.
State the governing wave rule: for a given frequency and medium, wave intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, $I \propto a^2$.
Take the square root of both sides: $a \propto \sqrt{1/r^2} = 1/r$. Amplitude falls more slowly than intensity.
Match $a \propto 1/r$ to the listed proportionality. This is option A.

options.B: This confuses amplitude with intensity, since intensity $I \propto 1/r^2$ but amplitude is proportional to the square root of intensity.
options.C: Amplitude must decrease with distance $r$ as the power spreads over area $4\pi r^2$, so it cannot increase as $r$.
options.D: Amplitude must decrease with distance $r$, and $r^2$ growth contradicts both energy spreading and $I \propto a^2$.
